description: Build the self-contained overlay module (src/overlay.ts) owned by BrowserSession, injected via context.addInitScript so it survives navigations and new pages, and re-back the existing highlight()/hideHighlight() with it. Implements the full DOM/visual layer for Tiers 1-4 plus a small typed server-side API the autopilot loop (FEAT-003) and mouse ops call. Also apply the snapshot speed work. Depends on FEAT-001 (config knobs + headed default + effective-headless tracking).
steps: Create src/overlay.ts. Export a BrowserOverlay class (or factory) that owns: (a) the client-side injected script string, and (b) a typed server-side API. The injected script runs INSIDE the page (self-contained, closes over nothing from Node), guarded to install exactly once per document (idempotent — check a window flag), and builds a fixed-position root container with a very high z-index and pointer-events:none so overlay nodes NEVER intercept real clicks or alter page behavior. It must expose a small window-level control object (e.g. window.__layaOverlay) with methods the server calls via page.evaluate.

Injection strategy: BrowserOverlay.install(context) calls context.addInitScript(<script>) so EVERY page/navigation/new tab re-injects the overlay automatically (fixing the navigation-fragile one-shot highlight). Also inject into any already-open page on first install (addInitScript only affects future loads) via page.evaluate for the current document. All server-side API methods (below) must be resilient: if window.__layaOverlay is missing (e.g. mid-navigation), they no-op/catch rather than throw.

Tier 1 (banner + cursor + ripple + spotlight): persistent top control banner reading '🤖 Laya is controlling this browser' with the dark HUD + purple accent (config.overlay.accent). Synthetic animated cursor element that travels to a target (moveCursor(x,y) with a CSS transition duration). Click ripple animation at a point (ripple(x,y)). Target spotlight/highlight that outlines an element region (spotlight(rect) or spotlight by ref) and hideSpotlight().

Tier 2 (popover/caption + HUD + progress + typing): action popover/caption near the cursor (toast/caption text like 'Clicking Sign in'). Live status HUD in the banner: setStatus(text), progress(step, maxSteps) rendering 'step N/max' + a progress bar, and setState('thinking'|'acting'|'success'|'error'|'uncertain') that swaps a label/icon (🤔 Deciding… vs ⚡ Acting…) and color. Optional character-by-character typing effect helper (used by the loop only when config.overlay.typingEffect is true; default off).

Tier 3 (scroll indicator + toasts + coloring + countdown): scroll indicator showing direction + position, transient toast(message, kind) notifications that auto-dismiss (navigation complete, dialog handled, tab opened/closed, error), success(green)/error(red)/uncertain(amber #f59e0b when confidence < threshold and escalating) coloring wired through setState, and a WAIT countdown ring/label countdown(ms) used only when config.overlay.waitCountdown is true (default off/lightweight).

Tier 4 (activity log + release hint + heartbeat + debug see-elements): collapsible on-page activity-log/feed panel with log(line) appending entries (enabled by config.overlay.activityLog, default on), a visible 'controlled by Laya — press Esc to release' affordance/hint, an idle heartbeat/breathing pulse on the banner toggled by setState('thinking') during long thinks, and a debug 'what the agent sees' mode (config.overlay.debugSeeElements) that briefly outlines all elements carrying data-laya-ref and shows their [ref=eN] label (reuse the refs capture() already stamps; do not re-walk the DOM independently — outline existing [data-laya-ref] nodes).

Define the typed server-side API on BrowserOverlay, each method acting on the ACTIVE page via page.evaluate and each wrapped so it never throws into the caller: setStatus(page,text), moveCursor(page,x,y), spotlight(page,ref|rect)/hideSpotlight(page), ripple(page,x,y), toast(page,message,kind), log(page,line), progress(page,step,max), setState(page,state), countdown(page,ms), scrollIndicator(page,direction,pos), showSeenElements(page)/hideSeenElements(page), and enable(bool)/isEnabled(). Prefer passing the active Page in, or have BrowserSession pass its active page. Add helper to compute an element's bounding rect for a given ref via the [data-laya-ref] selector so the loop can spotlight/move-cursor to a target by ref.

Wire into src/browser.ts: instantiate a BrowserOverlay from the session's resolved overlay config, and in launch(): after creating the context, if overlay is enabled call overlay.install(context). Guard on the EFFECTIVE headless mode from FEAT-001 when mode==='auto' (enabled only when actually headed OR forced 'on' — since visual verification runs headless, ensure the overlay STILL injects when explicitly forced on so tests can assert it headless). Re-back highlight(target)/hideHighlight() to delegate to overlay.spotlight/hideSpotlight when the overlay is active, keeping the existing method contract and the boolean return of highlight() (false when the ref matches nothing). When the overlay is disabled, retain a minimal working highlight (either keep the old inline-outline behavior or a no-overlay outline) so browser_highlight still functions.

Wire cursor/ripple into the raw mouse ops in browser.ts (mouseMove/mouseClick/mouseDrag) so vision-mode coordinate actions also move the synthetic cursor and ripple on click when the overlay is enabled — keep these calls best-effort and after the real Playwright action so they never change click behavior.

Snapshot speed work in src/snapshot.ts: in domWalk isVisible(), avoid the double forced reflow — read getBoundingClientRect() once and reuse it, and reorder so the cheap style checks (display/visibility/opacity) short-circuit before layout reads where possible; keep behavior identical (same elements selected). Consider a lighter capture path only if it does not change output. Do NOT change the ref numbering or the returned Control shape.

Post-action snapshot opt-out in src/tools/shared.ts / config: allow snapshotResult to honor a lighter/opt-out mode via config (e.g. a config.overlay-independent knob or reuse an existing config field) ONLY if it does not change default behavior — default must remain a full snapshot so existing tests and the benchmark are unaffected. If adding a knob, document it; if risky, limit this step to the domWalk reflow fix and note that in findings.
Keep everything ESM + typed; run npm run typecheck as you go.
acceptance_criteria: src/overlay.ts exists and exports a typed BrowserOverlay with the documented server-side API methods.
Overlay is injected via context.addInitScript so it re-appears after a navigation and on new tabs (verified in FEAT-004 tests).
All overlay root/child nodes have pointer-events:none and a very high z-index; a real click at an element covered by the banner still hits the underlying element (verified in FEAT-004).
highlight()/hideHighlight() still satisfy their existing contract (highlight returns false for a non-matching ref) and browser_highlight/browser_hide_highlight tools still work.
domWalk isVisible() no longer calls getBoundingClientRect() twice per element; snapshot output (controls, refs, visibleText) is unchanged for existing fixtures.
npm run typecheck clean; existing snapshot/assist/devtools tests still pass unchanged.
verification: Run `npm run test` — existing suites (snapshot.test.ts, assist.test.ts, devtools-tools.test.ts, core-tools.test.ts) still pass, confirming the overlay injection and snapshot changes did not regress capture output or tool contracts.
findings:
Implemented src/overlay.ts (BrowserOverlay) + integrated into src/browser.ts and applied the snapshot reflow ordering fix. File-by-file:

- src/overlay.ts (NEW): self-contained client script built as a string (buildClientScript) embedding a JSON options literal, closing over nothing from Node. Installs exactly once per document via window.__layaOverlayInstalled; ensureRoot() lazily builds a fixed-position root (#__laya_overlay__) with z-index 2147483646 and pointer-events:none on the root AND every child (mkDiv defaults pointerEvents:none). Tiers 1-4: banner '🤖 Laya is controlling this browser' (dark HUD + config accent), synthetic animated cursor moveCursor(x,y,caption) with CSS transition, click ripple, spotlight(rect)/hideSpotlight, action caption/popover, status HUD setStatus + progress(step,max) 'step N/max' + bar, setState(thinking/acting/success/error/uncertain) with '🤔 Deciding…' vs '⚡ Acting…' and colors (success green #22c55e, error red #ef4444, uncertain amber #f59e0b), scroll indicator, auto-dismissing toasts, WAIT countdown ring (gated by waitCountdown), collapsible activity-log panel with log(line) (gated by activityLog), 'controlled by Laya — press Esc to release' hint, idle heartbeat/breathing pulse on the dot while 'thinking', and debug see-elements (gated by debugSeeElements) that outlines existing [data-laya-ref] nodes and shows [ref=eN] labels (reuses capture()'s refs; does NOT re-walk). Server-side BrowserOverlay class: install(context, openPages) via context.addInitScript + evaluate into already-open pages; typed methods setStatus/setState/progress/moveCursor/ripple/spotlight(ref|rect)/hideSpotlight/toast/log/countdown/scrollIndicator/showSeenElements/hideSeenElements/refRect + enable/isEnabled/typingEffect. Every method routes through call() which no-ops when disabled/no page and swallows all errors so it NEVER throws into the caller (resilient to window.__layaOverlay missing mid-navigation). Typing effect exposed via getter (used only by loop when config.overlay.typingEffect).

- src/browser.ts: import BrowserOverlay; construct one from options.overlay (or a disabled fallback); getOverlay() exposes it to the loop (FEAT-003). In launch(), after creating context+page, resolve overlay against EFFECTIVE headless: mode 'on' => always inject (even headless, so FEAT-004 can assert headless), 'off' => never, 'auto' => only when headed; when active call overlay.install(context,[page]) so addInitScript covers future loads/tabs and the current page is injected too. highlight()/hideHighlight() re-backed to also drive overlay.spotlight/hideSpotlight when active while KEEPING the inline outline + the boolean contract (false when ref/selector matches nothing; verified). Mouse ops mouseMove/mouseClick/mouseDrag call overlay.moveCursor/ripple best-effort AFTER the real Playwright action so click/drag semantics never change.

- src/snapshot.ts: domWalk isVisible() clarified so cheap style checks (display/visibility/opacity) short-circuit BEFORE the single getBoundingClientRect() read (rect read at most once). Output (controls/refs/visibleText) unchanged; snapshot.test.ts passes unchanged. NOTE: the pre-existing code already called getBoundingClientRect() only once, so this is an ordering/comment clarification rather than removing a literal second call.

- src/tools/shared.ts: LEFT UNCHANGED per plan's risk guidance — default snapshot must stay full to keep existing tests + benchmark unaffected; limited snapshot speed work to the domWalk fix. No new opt-out knob added.

REAL TESTING (throwaway smoke scripts run against real headless chromium + fixture server, then deleted): 17/17 overlay checks passed — root injected, banner + Esc hint text, pointer-events:none on root+ALL children, z-index > 2e9, real element under the banner is hit-testable (overlay does not intercept), caption/progress 'step 2/5'/Deciding state/see-elements [ref=eN] rendered, refRect returns a rect, spotlight-by-ref, re-injection after navigation, re-injection on a new tab, highlight() false for non-matching ref + true for a matching selector, and server API no-ops (no throw) when window.__layaOverlay is deleted mid-session. A second guard script confirmed mode=auto headless => NOT injected, mode=off => NOT injected, mode=on => injected even headless. No bugs found beyond a test-ordering nuance (see-elements needs capture() to have stamped refs first, which is by design).

VERIFICATION: `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm run test` = 145 passed / 3 skipped (baseline preserved, only the 3 pre-existing skips); `npm run build` emits dist/. No overlay tests written here (that is FEAT-004). package-lock.json is a pre-existing untracked file, not part of this change; dist/ is gitignored.
